title: Kingdom of Africa
capsule: The Norman Kingdom of Africa (Regnum Africae) was a short-lived Sicilian dominion over the Ifriqiyan coast, established after Roger II of Sicily's admiral George of Antioch captured Mahdia from the Zirids on 22 June 1148, bringing the towns of Mahdia, Sfax, Sousse, Gabes, and Tripoli under Sicilian suzerainty. It functioned as a chain of tributary coastal enclaves that let Palermo command shipping and the grain trade across the Strait of Sicily rather than as a contiguous inland state. The advancing Almohad caliphate broke this network from the late 1150s: Tripoli fell in 1158 and Mahdia, the last Norman holdout, was besieged from 1159 and surrendered in January 1160, extinguishing the kingdom barely a dozen years after its founding under William I of Sicily.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political history and principal cities are documented in Norman-Sicilian and Arabic chronicles, but the extent of inland control and the status of towns during the Almohad pressure years are imprecisely mapped.
